idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy (v2.3.1), checkout-api began failing health checks in production (healthy=false, error rate ~18%) across us-east, us-west and eu-west. Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it was not used.) Rollback confirmed: all three regions now run v2.3.0. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. I rolled it back to v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. I didn't use v2.3.1-rc: it was only ever healthy in staging, so it doesn't meet that rule.
- **Check:** All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and on-call was paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the confirmed recovery, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before redeploying it.

content.text: The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0. v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it doesn't qualify.
